compatibility_rule: Components exchange `hello` frames listing supported protocol versions as MAJOR.MINOR strings. A peer accepts a message only if its MAJOR equals a supported MAJOR and its MINOR is less than or equal to the highest supported MINOR for that MAJOR. Unknown fields are rejected, not ignored. Incompatible peers receive error code PROTOCOL_INCOMPATIBLE with both version lists so the UI can tell the customer which component to update.

rules.terminal_result: Every command the controller sends is terminated by exactly one `result` frame per command_id (origin `agent` or `relay`). `error` frames are only used when no command_id is known (malformed frame, protocol error, subscription errors). Relay-side rejections before forwarding (signature, ownership, grant, rate limit, PC offline, queue full) are `result{origin:'relay', state:'failed', error}` and mean the PC never received the command. Once the relay has written a command to the agent's socket, nothing the relay observes can prove the command did not run: an agent connection lost after forwarding yields `result{origin:'relay', state:'outcome_unknown', error:OUTCOME_UNKNOWN}` whether or not an ack was seen; the agent's own journaled result may correct it once (see late_results). Clients therefore never present a relay `outcome_unknown` as 'nothing ran'.
rules.duplicate_command: An identical re-submission (same command_id, same signed payload bytes) is answered by re-emitting the previous `result` (or the current ack while still running). The same command_id with different payload bytes is rejected with COMMAND_ID_REUSED.
rules.command_window_and_confirmation: The command's issued_at/expires_at window is checked once when the PC receives the command. Once the PC has emitted confirmation_required, the challenge's expires_at governs: the signed confirmation is accepted iff the challenge is unexpired and unconsumed, and the command then proceeds regardless of its own expires_at. Controllers default disruptive commands to default_confirmed_command_lifetime_seconds so the two windows do not cross by accident.
rules.grants_snapshot: The PC's locally approved controller store (written only at local pairing approval) is the sole source of controller public keys. grants_snapshot is a revocation/intersection list: a kid is usable only if it is locally approved AND present in the latest snapshot; effective capabilities = local ∩ snapshot. A snapshot can never add a controller or widen a grant.
rules.challenge_text: A confirmation challenge travels as an opaque string (challenge_text). The PC stores the exact string it emitted; the relay validates it by strict-parsing a copy and forwards the original string verbatim; the controller strict-parses it once for display and hashes the string verbatim into challenge_digest.
rules.pairing_secret: The PC generates the pairing code locally. The backend only ever receives SHA-256 of the code as a lookup handle; the phone transfers the code out of band (QR or typing) and both devices derive the 6-digit verification code with HMAC-SHA256 keyed by the code, so a backend that substitutes a controller key cannot make the two displays agree.
rules.controller_socket_identity: A controller hello MUST carry kid and, to be bound, proof: an ES256 envelope signed by that key over a hello_proof payload {type, protocol_version, kid, account_id, issued_at, expires_at, nonce} (relay-frames#/$defs/hello_proof). The relay verifies the signature with the JWK of the controller row (session account, kid), checks envelope.kid == payload.kid == hello.kid, payload.account_id == the session's account, the time window (lifetime <= confirmation_challenge_lifetime_seconds, skew max_clock_skew_seconds) and that the nonce has not been seen before; only then does it bind the socket to the controller row and report hello_ack.controller_id. A hello without proof, or whose kid has no non-revoked controller row in the account, stays unbound (hello_ack without controller_id; such a socket may only poll pairing status via REST). A proof that is present but fails any check is answered with error UNKNOWN_KEY and close 4003. subscribe/command/confirmation/cancel require a bound, non-revoked controller; every envelope's kid must equal the socket's kid (else UNKNOWN_KEY and close 4003). Revocation sends `revoked` to all sockets bound to that controller and closes them. Controllers announce protocol_versions including 1.1 to use input_batch frames; 1.0 peers never receive them.
rules.state_cache: The relay keeps the last `state` frame per online PC and re-sends it (unchanged) after pc_status on every accepted subscribe. The agent sends a `state` frame immediately after applying grants_snapshot and then on change (debounced 500 ms) and every 30 s.
rules.in_flight: In-flight commands per PC = rows in created|accepted|executing|awaiting_confirmation. The relay gives each forwarded command a hard deadline = max(expires_at, received_at + timeout_ms) + (confirmation_challenge_lifetime_seconds if confirmation==challenge) + 10 s; at the deadline it emits result{origin:relay, state:outcome_unknown, error:OUTCOME_UNKNOWN} (the command was forwarded, so the relay cannot know whether it ran) and frees the slot. Armed power countdowns are exempt until fires_at + timeout_ms.
rules.late_results: After the relay closed a command as outcome_unknown, the agent's journaled result MAY be forwarded once as a correction result{origin:agent}; the controller treats it as replacing the prior outcome. A successful socket write is not delivery: on every reconnect the agent re-sends every terminal result that was never written to a socket and every terminal result finished after the last frame it received on the previous connection. Any other post-terminal result is dropped and logged.
rules.mismatch_handling: A command whose account_id/target_pc_id do not match the agent's stored identity is answered result{origin:agent, failed, ACCOUNT_MISMATCH|TARGET_PC_MISMATCH}, is NOT journaled, is logged as a local security event; three within 60 s make the agent close the socket and reconnect with backoff.
rules.agent_identity: The agent's pc_id/account_id are fixed at link time. If hello_ack.pc_id or grants_snapshot.pc_id/account_id differ, the agent closes the socket, stops reconnecting and shows a local re-link prompt. A command received before the connection's first grants_snapshot is answered result{failed, PC_RECONNECTING} and not journaled.
rules.plan_state: pc_enabled=false or controller status=plan_disabled in grants_snapshot are plan/account states, never revocations: local grants stay, the relay refuses routing (PC_PLAN_DISABLED / CONTROLLER_PLAN_DISABLED) and the agent refuses independently.
rules.token_and_entitlement_refresh: PC access tokens are validated only at WebSocket upgrade; an open socket is never closed for token expiry; the agent fetches a new token before reconnecting whenever less than 5 minutes remain. Entitlement assertions follow schemas/entitlement.schema.json: refreshed on connect and at 80% of lifetime; grace only on network error/5xx.
rules.pairing_offline: A claim against an offline PC is accepted (202, state claimed); the relay delivers pairing_request on the agent's next connect (after grants_snapshot) for every unexpired claimed session; the phone polls GET /v1/pairing/{pairing_id}. Pairing session, request and code share one expires_at.
rules.coalescing: Coalescing group = (coalesce key, canonical target JSON or '' when null) per PC across all controllers. The superseded command terminates as result{state:canceled, error:COMMAND_SUPERSEDED, result omitted} and is journaled as such.
rules.input_sessions: Manual touchpad/keyboard input (actions.json capabilities `pointer` and `keyboard`, both Free) is human-directed and travels in a bounded signed stream, not in commands. (1) Session: the controller sends the registry action input.session_start (permitted when its grant holds pointer or keyboard; params.takeover replaces another controller's session). The agent issues a fresh 22-character input_session_id and a lease of input_lease_seconds and answers input_session_result{input_session_id, lease_seconds, input_age_budget_ms, max_batch_events, pointer, keyboard, foreground_app?}. Exactly one controller owns a PC's session at a time; a second controller without takeover gets INPUT_SESSION_OWNED. Takeover, controller revocation, grant narrowing, pc switching, remote-control disable, Windows session lock, a secure desktop, lease expiry, agent restart or the relay losing the controller's socket END the session: the agent first retires the session id so delayed batches cannot press anything, then releases every button and key THAT SESSION injected (never the physical keyboard's), then sends input_session{event:ended, reason, holds_released}. (2) Batches: each controller_input_batch frame carries an envelope signed by the controller key over input_batch_payload{type:input_batch, protocol_version, account_id, controller_id, target_pc_id, input_session_id, seq, issued_at, expires_at, events[<= input_batch_max_events]} with expires_at - issued_at <= input_batch_lifetime_seconds. The relay verifies the signature with the socket's key record, binds account/controller, requires a live grant whose capabilities cover every event type (pointer_* need pointer; text/key/shortcut need keyboard; INPUT_NOT_PERMITTED), requires the PC online and past its first snapshot (PC_OFFLINE / PC_RECONNECTING), applies plans.json input_rate_limit per controller (RATE_LIMITED), forwards the envelope verbatim and keeps NO commands row and NO security event per accepted batch. The agent re-verifies the signature against its local grant, requires input_session_id to be the live session owned by this controller (INPUT_SESSION_REQUIRED / INPUT_SESSION_EXPIRED), requires seq strictly greater than the last accepted seq (INPUT_SEQUENCE_INVALID: the batch is dropped, the session continues), requires the batch's age <= input_age_budget_ms, where age is measured against the controller's clock offset estimated per session (the minimum of receipt time minus issued_at over a recent window, seeded at input.session_start) so that phone/PC clock skew neither blocks input nor defeats the check; the relay's received_at stamp bounds the relay-to-agent leg the same way (INPUT_STALE: the batch is dropped) and renews the lease on every valid batch (an empty events array is a pure keepalive). Rejections are counted in input_ack.dropped_events and reported to the batch's controller as error{error, ref_pc_id, ref_input_session_id}: the agent sends error{error, ref_input_session_id, ref_controller_id} (at most one per code per second), the relay checks that ref_controller_id belongs to the PC's account, strips it, adds ref_pc_id and delivers the frame only to that controller's protocol-1.1 sockets. Input rejections never terminate a command. (3) Dispatch: adjacent pointer_move events within a batch may be summed; nothing is ever merged across a button, scroll, text, key or shortcut event, and ordering is preserved. If dispatch falls behind by more than input_age_budget_ms the agent discards pending events, suspends the session (input_session{event:suspended, reason:backpressure}) and requires a fresh input.session_start. Old traffic is never replayed after a reconnect or restart; the journal is not used for input. (4) Acks: the agent sends input_ack{input_session_id, last_seq, accepted_events, dropped_events, held_buttons, held_keys} at most four times per second while a session is live; it reports Windows acceptance, never an observed application effect. (5) Content: text events are literal customer input; no component logs, journals, persists, or forwards them to an AI provider, and the relay sees them only in transit (TLS, not end-to-end). AI and routines cannot use pointer, keyboard, text, key or shortcut primitives (rules.ai_eligibility).
rules.grant_update: The PC's local approval is the only source of a controller's capabilities. When the owner changes a grant locally (for example grants pointer and keyboard to an already-paired phone, or removes them), the agent sends grant_update{controller_id, kid, capabilities}; the relay replaces the grant row's capabilities with exactly that list (it may widen or narrow), re-pushes grants_snapshot and the account's device list reflects it. Existing grants never gain pointer or keyboard implicitly: the capabilities are absent until the PC owner adds them. grants_snapshot remains an intersection list and cannot add capabilities the PC did not store.
rules.ai_eligibility: Actions with ai_eligible:false (every input.* action) and the input_batch primitives never enter an AI provider's tool catalogue, a saved routine or a layout shortcut. Typing literal text through the keyboard capability is UI input to whatever the PC has focused; it is not parsed by the deterministic text-command parser or any model and never invokes shell execution inside the agent.
